reading_guide: an example is a place to go and look: map, the sector to stand in, and the object's own index
examples are taken one map at a time, in map order, so they are spread across the campaign and are not a ranking
read_as and worked_by are `bloodmap.effects`' reading of the moving sectors of that type; a name from where a thing sits, never from its type
an effect is defined by the XSECTOR fields listed under `fields` and by nothing else
cited_by is library code whose docstring names the lesson
a channel entry counts who sends on and who listens to one of the engine's reserved channels; its examples are the senders
an example's place, and an entry's places, are ids of places-v1.json: the rooms holding the most of it, most first. A null place is a sector no catalogued room claims

every entry is a PART. `wiring` is the mechanisms: each row is one shape of chain, a cause on a sender and what answers, counted over the campaign; a sector that answers is named by what `bloodmap.effects` reads it doing to the space, where it reads one
set_off_by and drives on a part are counted over those chains; a part with neither is never on a wire in the campaign
a row's `silent` is how many of its chains start at a sender that reports neither its ON nor its OFF change, so never sends: wired, and inert
a row's `through_closet` is how many of its chains pass through a relay in a sector no player reaches: the campaign's way of building a cascade
